title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continuing pp. 81-83). X is a variety over a field K ⊂ ℂ, with Γ = Gal(K̄/K). Π_1(X) is the topological fundamental groupoid of X(ℂ), and Π̂_1(X) is its profinite completion. Π̂_1(X) has a purely scheme-theoretic description, so Γ acts on the full subgroupoid on X(K̄). On the full subgroupoid on X(K), Γ fixes the objects. It therefore acts on each Hom-set, and for a path ℓ one gets 'defect' elements f_ℓ(u), g_ℓ(u) (u ∈ Γ), roughly ᵘℓ = ℓ·f_ℓ(u) or ᵘℓ = g_ℓ(u)·ℓ. These measure how far the discrete path ℓ is from being Galois-fixed. The previous page showed that a K-morphism f: X → Y is compatible with all this, formulas (39) and (40).

This page:
(i) Special case: f an isomorphism, and especially X = Y with f in a group G of K-automorphisms of X. Then G acts on Π_1(X) and on its full subgroupoids on X(K̄) and on X(K). Because the elements of G are defined over K, their action commutes with Γ, so G×Γ acts on Π̂_1(X) and on its restrictions to X(K̄) and X(K). On the objects of the X(K)-part, Γ acts trivially but G in general does not; G permutes the rational base points.
(ii) Reduction to finite data. Choose x_0 ∈ X(K) and a set I ⊂ X(K) of base points ('sommets') containing x_0. Restricted to I, the Γ-action on the groupoid Π̂_1(X,I) is determined by two pieces of data:
- its action on the vertex group π̂_1(X,x_0);
- its action on the right π̂_1(X,x_0)-torsors Hom_{Π̂_1(X,I)}(x_0,x_i), i ∈ I (formula (41)).
The reason: every arrow x_i → x_j factors through x_0, and the torsor action is semilinear over the group action. Equivalently (p. 85), it suffices to know f_{l_i}(u) for one chosen discrete path l_i from x_0 to x_i. These form a family of 1-cocycles Γ → π̂_1(X,x_0) for the twisted Galois action. One also needs f_{λ_j}(u) or g_{λ_j}(u) for discrete generators λ_j of π_1(X,x_0).
The next page criticises this description because it depends on arbitrary choices (base point, paths, generators). It is especially unsuitable when a symmetry group G acts and I is chosen G-stable. This motivates the base-point-free, symmetric groupoid viewpoint of the 'Teichmüller tower' programme.
errors: No mathematical error. A minor implicit point: 'the action is known' should be read as determined by the action on π̂_1(X,x_0) together with one cocycle value per torsor (ᵘ(l_i·γ) = ᵘl_i·ᵘγ). This holds only because I ⊂ X(K), so Γ fixes the objects. For non-rational base points the torsors are permuted and the description changes.
The sentence 'le groupe opère par trivialement sur les ...' is garbled in the manuscript. The intended meaning is that Γ (not G) acts trivially on the objects of the X(K)-groupoid.

ideas.what: Galois action on the profinite fundamental groupoid restricted to K-rational base points, encoded by path-defect elements f_ℓ(u), g_ℓ(u) (1-cocycles)
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on étale fundamental groupoid with several rational base points; path torsors and Galois cocycles (as in Ihara's and Deligne's treatment of P^1 minus 3 points)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (1980s), Deligne 1989 (Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points)
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (fundamental groupoid, Galois action in general form); Esquisse d'un programme (1984) and La Longue Marche (1981) for the multi-base-point groupoid viewpoint

ideas.what: Combined action of G×Γ on Π̂_1(X) for G a group of K-automorphisms; Γ fixes rational vertices while G permutes them
ideas.modern_name: Equivariant Galois action on fundamental groupoids with symmetry; symmetric base-point sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse); later Drinfeld, Ihara, Nakamura and Schneps in the Grothendieck–Teichmüller setting
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (§ on the Teichmüller tower; groupoids with base points stable under symmetries)

ideas.what: Reduction of the groupoid action on Π̂_1(X,I) to the action on one vertex group plus the action on the path torsors Hom(x_0,x_i)
ideas.modern_name: Connected groupoid is equivalent to its vertex group plus torsor data; Galois action described by an outer action lifted plus cocycles

deep.surprise_reason: A routine working-out of how a Galois action on a fundamental groupoid with rational base points is determined by finite data. The G×Γ-symmetric viewpoint and the dissatisfaction with base-point choices are exactly the themes Grothendieck later published in the Esquisse and that Ihara, Deligne, Drinfeld and others developed.
transcription_corrections: 'Cette fois-ci le groupe opère par trivialement sur les éléments [?]' — the illegible word is likely 'sommets' (vertices/objects): Γ acts trivially on the objects of Π_1(X_K).
'et un ensemble [?]' likely reads 'et un ensemble de sommets I ⊂ X_K contenant x_0'.
Formula (41) should read Hom_{Π̂_1(X,I)}(x_0, x_i), i ∈ I: the torsors of paths from x_0 to x_i.
